question: Visualize patient transitions between disease stages (I, II, III, IV) across three time points (T1, T2, T3) using a Sankey diagram. Flow width should be proportional to the number of patients making each transition.

files.eval_guideline: Sankey diagram must show patient transitions between disease stages across T1, T2, and T3 with flow widths proportional to patient counts; color scheme and node ordering may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The files have identical base names and PNG image formats, and both correspond directly to the requested disease-stage transition Sankey diagram.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires semantic features of the visualization—correct stages and time points, transitions, and flow widths proportional to patient counts—while explicitly allowing visual differences in colors and node ordering. A semantic comparison is therefore more appropriate than pixel-level matching.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images present the same Sankey diagram of patient movement among disease stages I–IV across T1, T2, and T3. The node totals and flow widths agree: T1 totals are 38, 41, 29, and 12; T2 totals are 31, 40, 32, and 17; and T3 totals are 28, 36, 35, and 21. The candidate makes the underlying transition counts explicit, including T1→T2 flows of Stage I: 25/10/3, Stage II: 4/28/9, Stage III: 2/2/20/5, and Stage IV: 12, plus T2→T3 flows of Stage I: 25/6, Stage II: 3/30/7, Stage III: 28/4, and Stage IV: 17. These values match the proportional flows visible in the reference. Differences are presentational only: the candidate adds count annotations, time-point headings, totals, and a legend, uses somewhat different color saturation and typography, and places some labels outside nodes. These changes improve interpretability without altering the data or scientific message.
